column1: # The decomposition, as data: one line per unit `run.sh` must decide.
#   <unit>  <planning artifact id that owns it>  <what a green row means>
# Tab-separated. Order is dependency order, so a reader of a red table meets the root cause first.
# It is a file rather than an array inside `run.sh` for one reason: `check-checks-runner.sh` has to
# run the runner against a synthetic decomposition to show N2-N5 without recursing into this one.
# A list the runner reads is a list a test can substitute; a list compiled into it is not.

column3: the runner names every unit, fails a missing check, prints its table on every path
scan-declarations.sh emits the tree's document-declared surfaces, sorted and byte-stable
the audit exists at the guide path, the guide routes to it, and its corpus list equals the globs
exactly one table, the seven columns in order, every verdict open or closed, a non-vacuous floor
every open row's three trailing cells hold an em dash, never a blank or a hedge
every closed row states a guarantee and an anchor an adopter can follow somewhere other than here
every unsettled closed row names a planning artifact that resolves in the store
every Invited at fragment is at the line it cites, and every Decided by line settles its verdict
the relation vocabulary gets one row per layer, never one averaged verdict
every scan candidate has a row, every non-scanned row has a resolving citation, and the limit is stated
the audit states how it was produced, and every command it names runs
writes stay under docs/ and .engineering/, and no check reads a planning body
nine deliberate mutations each turn a named check red, on a copy, with the tree untouched
